thread:
rami: Quick FYI — spotted a couple of copy/paste traps in the quickstart during onboarding lab runthrough.
rami: Two things: the README uses a backslash-multiline curl that breaks in PowerShell, and the examples use inconsistent env var names (we have REDWOOD_API, REDWOOD_KEY, and REDWOOD_API_KEY all floating around).
rami: Problematic curl from README:
```
curl \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"hey\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
rami: If you paste that into PowerShell it blows up with `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: -H` or treats the backslashes literally.
tasha: Oh nice catch. We should do two things: switch to a single-line curl for portability, and add a PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod example. Also pick one canonical env var name.
evan: Agreed. I'd vote for REDWOOD_API_KEY as canonical. For TS/JS snippets we should also standardize on process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY and show both import styles (default vs named) because many folks have different tsconfig flags.
evan: Proposed README edits:
Single-line curl (portable):
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
PowerShell variant:
```
$headers = @{ Authorization = \"Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY\"; \"Content-Type\" = \"application/json\" }
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -Method Post -Headers $headers -Body '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```
evan: For TypeScript note: show both imports and add a tiny comment about esModuleInterop. Example: `import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference' // if you enable esModuleInterop` and `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference' // works without esModuleInterop`.
rami: Can someone open a docs PR? Also, can we add a minimal docs smoke test that runs a small node script (docs/examples/quickstart-smoke.js) in docs CI so copy/paste regressions fail fast?
tasha: I'll open the PR and add the smoke script. Plan: update README, update examples/quickstart to use REDWOOD_API_KEY, add docs/examples/quickstart-smoke.js which just reads the env var and prints a success line (no network call). Also add a lightweight grep-based linter in docs CI to assert README uses REDWOOD_API_KEY.
docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/702 — normalizes env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY, replaces multiline curl with single-line + PowerShell, adds TS import note, and adds docs smoke script + CI lint job.
evan: Nice. Can we also file a follow-up to sweep other language samples (python, go, ruby) for env var parity? I'll do that after this PR merges.
tasha: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/248 (sample parity sweep).
rami: Thanks! Once PR merges I'll update the onboarding checklist to reference the canonical env var and the PowerShell note.
